limitations: Synthetic same-platform workloads, not a universal pipeline speedup or RAM guarantee. Control workloads and regressions are retained; do not extrapolate peak results to all data.
All ratios compare current production directly with the original commit. Historical per-pass ratios are neither multiplied nor added.
Five observations per revision and workload are reported individually; small timing/RSS changes, especially startup-scale measurements, can reflect noise.

A revision's initial median wall time exceeded 0.05 seconds and either max/min exceeded 1.6 or median/min exceeded 1.2. These four workloads were rerun after browser authorization activity finished. Use the complete rerun regardless of its speedup; retain the initial observations as exploratory.
C++ benchmark binaries use normal clocks. Existing fixed-clock CLI regressions separately verify exact diagnostics/RNG behavior; normal benchmark elapsed-time diagnostics can differ.
PCA uses matching builds and the same Accelerate library with VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1; no cross-library equivalence claim.

Perl has one complete annotate CLI workload and five actual-source API workloads. The phased-join driver does not establish tabix/indexed-file CLI integration; baseline nondeterminism outside this fixed environment remains.
LD metadata rejection skips genotype decoding, not physical payload reads. No whole-file genotype cache is introduced.
The original undefined behavior, integer overflow, resource-exhaustion timing, floating-trap timing and untested platforms remain outside finite byte-equivalence evidence.
